note: Subjects/9701 Chemistry/02 Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry/2.1 Relative masses of atoms and molecules.md
outline: The unified atomic mass unit is one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. Relative isotopic mass describes one isotope; $A_r$ is a weighted mean for an element. $M_r$ compares one molecule with the unit; relative formula mass compares one formula unit. All relative masses are ratios and have no units.

misconceptions.statement: The unified atomic mass unit is the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
misconceptions.refutation: It is one twelfth of that mass.
misconceptions.contrast: A carbon-12 atom has mass 12 unified atomic mass units.

misconceptions.statement: Relative atomic mass is the mass of one isotope.
misconceptions.refutation: It is the weighted mean mass of atoms of an element, allowing for isotopic abundance.
misconceptions.contrast: Relative isotopic mass refers to one isotope.

misconceptions.statement: An ionic compound has a relative molecular mass.
misconceptions.refutation: An ionic lattice has no discrete molecules; use relative formula mass.
misconceptions.contrast: Use relative molecular mass for a molecule and relative formula mass for a formula unit.

misconceptions.statement: The subscript in a molecular formula can be ignored when finding relative mass.
misconceptions.refutation: Each atom in the formula contributes its relative atomic mass.
misconceptions.contrast: For $\ce{O2}$, add the masses of two oxygen atoms.

misconceptions.statement: Relative isotopic mass carries the unit u, just like the mass of an atom.
misconceptions.refutation: Relative isotopic mass is an atomic mass divided by one unified atomic mass unit; the units cancel.
misconceptions.contrast: An atomic mass of $19.99u$ corresponds to a relative isotopic mass of 19.99 without a unit.

misconceptions.statement: One unified atomic mass unit is defined as the mass of one proton or one hydrogen atom.
misconceptions.refutation: The unified atomic mass unit is defined as one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
misconceptions.contrast: A hydrogen atom has a mass close to one unified atomic mass unit, but hydrogen is not the defining reference.
misconceptions.source: SaveMyExams/9701 a-level-chemistry-cie-25/9701 c2.1.pdf p.2; Cambridge 9701 June 2022 P21 Q1(e)(i), https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/567189-june-2022-mark-scheme-paper-21.pdf

worked.problem: A sample contains only two isotopes with relative isotopic masses 34.97 and 36.97, at abundances of 75% and 25% respectively. Calculate its relative atomic mass.

steps.why: The two isotopes account for every atom in this sample.
Each isotope contributes in proportion to the fraction of atoms that belong to it; an equal average would assume equal abundances.
Dividing the percentage-weighted total by 100 gives the mean relative mass.

steps.do: Report $A_r=35.47$, without a unit; it lies between 34.97 and 36.97, closer to 34.97.
steps.why: Relative mass is a ratio, and the more abundant lighter isotope pulls the mean towards its mass.

faded.problem: A second sample contains only isotopes of relative isotopic masses 34.97 and 36.97, at abundances 60% and 40% respectively. The abundances total 100%. Complete the weighting and calculate the relative atomic mass.

A sample of an element contains only two isotopes with relative isotopic masses 20.0 and 22.0. Their percentage abundances are [[p]]% and [[q]]% respectively. Calculate the relative atomic mass of the sample.
items.explanation: Weight each relative isotopic mass by its percentage abundance: $A_r=(20.0\times[[p]]+22.0\times[[q]])/100$, with no unit. The unweighted mean 21.0 would apply only to equal isotope abundances.
hints: Which isotope contributes more atoms to the sample?
Multiply each relative isotopic mass by its percentage abundance, add, then divide by the total percentage.
Start with $20.0\times[[p]]$ for the lighter isotope and form the corresponding contribution for the heavier isotope.

items.stem: An atom of a specified isotope has a mass of $19.99u$. Identify the statement that correctly distinguishes its mass from its relative isotopic mass.

options.A: Its mass is $19.99u$; its relative isotopic mass is 19.99 with no unit.
options.B: Its mass is $19.99u$; its relative isotopic mass is $19.99u$.
options.C: Its mass is 19.99 with no unit; its relative isotopic mass is $19.99u$.
options.D: Its mass is $19.99u$; its relative isotopic mass is $19.99/12$ with no unit.

items.explanation: Relative isotopic mass is the ratio $19.99u/(1u)=19.99$, so the units cancel while the actual atomic mass retains $u$. Dividing by 12 again incorrectly uses the mass of a whole carbon-12 atom as the reference.
hints: Distinguish a measured mass from a ratio of two masses.
Write relative isotopic mass as the mass of the isotope atom divided by one unified atomic mass unit.
In the ratio, track what happens when the same mass unit appears in both numerator and denominator.

flashcards.front: Define the unified atomic mass unit.
flashcards.back: One twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
The weighted mean mass of an atom of an element relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
The mass of an atom of an isotope relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
The mass of a molecule relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
The mass of a formula unit relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.

9701-2.1.1.motivate: An atom is too light for everyday mass units to be convenient. A common reference lets us compare atomic masses directly.
9701-2.1.1.establish: The unified atomic mass unit, $u$, is defined as one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom. Thus one carbon-12 atom has a mass of exactly $12u$. The definition selects a particular isotope, carbon-12, rather than an average carbon atom. Actual atomic masses may be expressed in $u$; relative masses are ratios to $u$ and have no units.
9701-2.1.1.connect: This fixed carbon-12 reference is the denominator in the definitions of relative isotopic, atomic, molecular and formula mass.
9701-2.1.1.note:
- One unified atomic mass unit is one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
- One carbon-12 atom has mass exactly $12u$.
- Relative masses are unitless ratios to this reference.
9701-2.1.1.self_explain: Why does one carbon-12 atom have a mass of exactly $12u$?

discover.stem: One carbon-12 atom has a mass of exactly $12u$. What fraction of that atom's mass is $1u$?
discover.explanation: Divide the mass of one carbon-12 atom into twelve equal parts; each part is $1u$.

9701-2.1.1.plain_words: The unified atomic mass unit, $u$, is one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom. Use $u$ as the reference for atomic masses, so one carbon-12 atom has a mass of exactly $12u$. A mass compared with $u$ is a unitless ratio.

terms.meaning: The isotope of carbon with mass number 12, chosen as the standard for the unit.
A mass divided by the unified atomic mass unit; it is a ratio, so it has no units.

forms.name: Define the unified atomic mass unit
wordings: Define the unified atomic mass unit
State what is meant by one unified atomic mass unit
forms.example:
**Define:** the unified atomic mass unit.

- Name the quantity: a mass unit for atoms, symbol $u$.
- Give the reference: the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
- Give the fraction: one twelfth.
- Model answer: one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
forms.check: State the mass of one carbon-12 atom in unified atomic mass units.
forms.answer: 12 u. Since 1 u is one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom, one carbon-12 atom has mass exactly 12 u.
forms.source: SaveMyExams notes 9701 c2.1, p.2; bundle 9701-2.1.1. Example and check authored independently.

rubric.point: Gives the mass of one carbon-12 atom as 12 u.

retry.check: One carbon-12 atom has a mass of $1.992\times10^{-26}$ kg. Using $1u=1.66\times10^{-27}$ kg, calculate the mass of this atom in $u$.
retry.answer: Divide: $1.992\times10^{-26}/1.66\times10^{-27}=12.0$, so the atom has a mass of $12.0u$.

rubric.point: Divides the given mass by $1.66\times10^{-27}$ kg.

misconceptions.idea: The unified atomic mass unit is the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
misconceptions.temptation: Both mention carbon-12, so the unit and the atom look interchangeable.
misconceptions.fix: It is one twelfth of that mass. One carbon-12 atom has mass 12 u.

misconceptions.idea: One unified atomic mass unit is the mass of one proton or one hydrogen atom.
misconceptions.temptation: Hydrogen is the lightest atom, and 1 u looks about that size.
misconceptions.fix: The unit is defined from carbon-12. A hydrogen atom has a mass close to 1 u, but the definition does not refer to hydrogen.

9701-2.1.2.motivate: A symbol, isotope label, molecule and ionic formula refer to different entities. Naming the mass correctly tells the examiner which entity you mean.
9701-2.1.2.establish: Relative isotopic mass is the mass of one atom of a specified isotope relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom. Relative atomic mass, $A_r$, is the weighted mean mass of an atom of an element relative to that reference; isotope abundances determine the weighting. Relative molecular mass, $M_r$, is the mass of one molecule relative to the reference. Relative formula mass is the mass of one formula unit relative to the reference, used for ionic compounds without discrete molecules. Add the constituent $A_r$ values, respecting subscripts, to calculate molecular or formula mass. These are relative ratios without units.
9701-2.1.2.connect: The choice of entity determines the term: an element has $A_r$, a named isotope has relative isotopic mass, a molecule has $M_r$, and an ionic formula unit has relative formula mass.
9701-2.1.2.note:
- Relative isotopic mass concerns one atom of one isotope.
- $A_r$ is the abundance-weighted mean for atoms of an element.
- $M_r$ concerns one molecule; relative formula mass concerns one formula unit.
- Each is measured relative to one twelfth of a carbon-12 atom's mass and has no unit.
9701-2.1.2.self_explain: Why is 35.5 appropriate for chlorine's $A_r$ but not for the relative isotopic mass of chlorine-35?

discover.stem: Consider, in order: chlorine-35 atoms; chlorine containing a mixture of isotopes; water molecules; sodium chloride formula units. Which sequence names their appropriate relative masses?
discover.explanation: A named isotope uses relative isotopic mass; an element with mixed isotopes uses weighted relative atomic mass. Water consists of molecules, whereas ionic sodium chloride is represented by formula units.

9701-2.1.2.plain_words: Name the entity before naming the mass. A single isotope has relative isotopic mass. An element with several isotopes has relative atomic mass, $A_r$, which is a weighted mean. A molecule has relative molecular mass, $M_r$, and an ionic formula unit has relative formula mass. Each is a ratio with no units.

terms.meaning: The mass of one atom of a particular isotope, compared with one twelfth of a carbon-12 atom.
The weighted mean mass of the atoms of an element, compared with $u$; the isotope abundances set the weighting.
The mass of one molecule of a molecular compound, compared with $u$; the sum of the relative atomic masses in the molecular formula.
The same calculation as $M_r$, applied to one formula unit of an ionic compound.
The simplest formula of a compound, such as $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ for silicon dioxide.

forms.name: Name the correct relative mass
wordings: Identify the correct relative mass for the entity
Define relative isotopic mass or relative atomic mass
forms.example:
**Which term?** Name the relative mass for each entity.

- Chlorine-35 atoms, a single isotope: relative isotopic mass.
- Sodium chloride, which has no discrete molecules: relative formula mass.
- Name the entity first, then choose the matching term.
forms.check: A sample of bromine contains $^{79}$Br and $^{81}$Br atoms. Name the correct relative mass for the element bromine in this sample.
forms.answer: Relative atomic mass, $A_r$. The sample has more than one isotope, so the weighted mean over the isotopes is needed.
forms.source: SaveMyExams notes 9701 c2.1, pp.2–3 (definitions); example and check authored independently.

rubric.point: Explains that the isotopes are weighted by abundance, so a weighted mean is needed.

retry.check: Name the correct relative mass for one atom of $^{85}$Rb.
retry.answer: Relative isotopic mass, because one atom of one named isotope is involved.

rubric.point: Says the question concerns one atom of one isotope.

forms.name: Calculate a relative mass from given data
wordings: Calculate the relative atomic mass from the isotopic abundances
Calculate the relative formula mass of the compound
forms.example:
**Calculate** $A_r$ of boron, given $^{10}$B at 20% and $^{11}$B at 80%.

- Multiply each mass number by its percentage abundance: $10\times20$ and $11\times80$.
- Add the products: $200+880=1080$.
- Divide by 100: $A_r=10.8$.

For a compound, add the relative atomic masses of every atom in the formula. For $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$: $40.1+2(16.0)+2(1.0)=74.1$.
forms.check: A sample of magnesium contains $^{24}$Mg (79%), $^{25}$Mg (10%) and $^{26}$Mg (11%). Calculate the relative atomic mass of magnesium in this sample to three significant figures.
forms.source: SaveMyExams notes 9701 c2.1, pp.2–3 (weighted average and $M_r$ method); example and check authored independently. Abundances are illustrative.

rubric.point: Multiplies each mass number by its percentage abundance.
Divides the total by 100 to give 24.3.

retry.check: Calculate the relative formula mass of aluminium sulfate, $\mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3}$, using $A_r$ values Al 27.0, S 32.1 and O 16.0.

rubric.point: Counts 2 aluminium, 3 sulfur and 12 oxygen atoms.

misconceptions.idea: Relative atomic mass is the mass of one isotope.
misconceptions.temptation: An element's symbol names one kind of atom, so one isotope's mass seems enough.
misconceptions.fix: Relative atomic mass is the weighted mean over the isotopes present; relative isotopic mass refers to one isotope.

misconceptions.idea: The subscript in a molecular formula can be ignored when finding relative mass.
misconceptions.temptation: The subscript looks like a small counting detail, so one atom per symbol seems enough.
misconceptions.fix: Each atom in the formula adds its relative atomic mass; $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ contains two O atoms and two H atoms.
